Performers
London Symphony Orchestra (orchestra), London Philharmonic Choir (choir), Hermann Scherchen (conductor), Frederick Jackson (chorus master), Thomas Matthews (orchestral leader), George Eskdale (trumpet) Documented

The complete-set soloists are Margaret Ritchie, Constance Shacklock (spelt Schacklock on Commons), William Herbert and Richard Standen. They are not presented as vocal soloists in this chorus.

[1] [4]
Work version
The cited Westminster issue describes the performance as based on the original Dublin performance of 13 April 1742. Documented

This is the record’s own description, not a score-collation result. No editor is named; numbering varies between the digital file and this issue.

[4]
Recorded
1953 Documented

Commons gives 1 January 1953 and repeats it as structured inception. The embedded DATE gives only 1953; no session log corroborates the day or month, which are therefore not adopted.

[1] [3]
Place
London Documented

The discographic entry transcribes “Recorded by Westminster in London”; no venue is stated.

[4]
Label
Westminster; a Nixa recording Documented[1] [4]
Catalogue
XWN 3306 — documented 1957 reissue Documented

The physical edition used for the Commons transfer is not established.

[4]
Matrix, take, sides
Hallelujah is side E, track 5 on Westminster XWN 3306. Documented

That set is auto-coupled: sides 1/6, 2/5 and 3/4. No matrix or take number, nor proof that this pressing supplied the stream, was recovered.

[4]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

No transfer or restoration engineer is credited in the consulted sources.

[1] [3]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is documented; upload and encoding-software dates are not session or transfer dates.

[1] [3]
Processing
Embedded encoder: Lavf57.83.100. Commons master: Ogg Vorbis, 44.1 kHz, 1 channel. Documented

These are file properties, not evidence of noise reduction, equalisation, pitch correction or other restoration. Earlier processing is not documented.

[3]
Composition rights
Original composition and eighteenth-century English libretto are public domain in the United States. Inferred, not documented

The original complete score was published in 1767; this does not determine rights in a later edition or recording.

[6] [7]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis). Documented

Commons applies PD-EU-audio to Scherchen’s Westminster recording and dates it to 1953; no exact session day is inferred. Usable under the programme’s pre-1963 European sound-recording rule; the former 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US sound-recording status is not established. A recording date alone is not represented as an independently verified first-publication date.

[10] [11] [12]

London Symphony Orchestra and London Philharmonic Choir; Hermann Scherchen, conductor; Frederick Jackson, chorus master. Westminster source, via Wikimedia Commons. Commons asserts EU public-domain recording status (PD-EU-audio); rights elsewhere are not established. Rights statement
